meta.title: UEFN Game Device Advisor - Decision Logic
meta.description: Rules-engine style decision logic: pick a genre, answer a short sequence of follow-up questions, and the engine unions together the resulting device list + key settings. This is the source-of-truth data model intended to drive an interactive tool (web form, in-app wizard, etc.).
how_it_works: Step 1: 'What type of game do you want to make?' — the user picks one of 10 top-level game categories.

Step 2: 'Which one exactly?' — they pick an exact game type within that category (or 'Just give me the basics' for the category's essential devices only). Game types are 'live' (fully researched) or 'draft' (visible only in development mode; resolves to the category baseline device set until researched).
Step 3: The tool walks the ordered 'questions' list for that game type, one at a time.

Step 4: The user picks a Brand Template (Original, or a licensed IP) — this determines the starter asset pack available in their island, and highlights brands that suit the chosen game type. It does not change which devices the game needs mechanically.

Step 5: A restriction-confirmation screen summarizes that brand's usage rules (revenue share, asset limits, content restrictions) with a link to the full official guidelines, before confirming or going back.
Step 6: A Summary screen shows the game type's core loop as a circular diagram (entry point → repeating loop → win/lose outcomes), a recap of all choices, and a Name + Save (to localStorage) control.

Step 7: Before the build steps, an experience-level screen (Complete beginner / Some experience / Experienced / Expert) is asked fresh every time (never saved with the game). Anyone other than Complete beginner skips the Basic Navigation step.

Step 8: A 4-or-5-step build walkthrough (Basic Navigation only for Complete beginners): Create Your Project, [Basic Navigation], Block Out Your Island, Add Your Core Game Loop Devices, Make It Look Good — each with a video slot.

Devices live in a shared device_library keyed by device name (each with exact UEFN Details-panel settings). Game types reference devices by name; the final list merges universal_devices + the category baseline (for types that inherit it) + the game type's own devices + anything added by question answers, de-duplicated.
Each device carries a 'category' tag (see meta.categories) so the results screen groups devices by role.
Setting names and values reflect the ACTUAL UEFN Details panel property names and dropdown options (researched from Epic's official documentation).

Development mode (header toggle, persisted): off = only live game types are selectable; on = drafts appear too, badged with what hasn't been researched yet. Saved games always load regardless of the toggle.

logo.notes: Square brand logo/icon used on the small selection tiles. Keep the mark centred with ~10% padding inside the square so it doesn't touch the edges. Oversized at 160px so it stays sharp on high-DPI screens.

hero.notes: Wide key-art banner shown at the top of the brand detail panel. 8:3 is a third shorter than a standard 16:9 frame, so compose for a letterbox crop rather than a full scene. Avoid putting important detail or text in the outer 5% since it is cropped with object-fit: cover on narrow windows.

brand_image_spec.location: Save both files in an 'images/brands' folder next to uefn_game_wizard.html, named <brand_id>_logo.png and <brand_id>_hero.jpg.

NOTE: https://create.fortnite.com/news/ip-partner-fee-schedule is stale — it omits Star Wars and KPop Demon Hunters entirely, and incorrectly implies Star Wars does not support in-island transactions. The per-brand rules pages are authoritative. brand_templates.label: Original (No Brand Template)
brand_templates.description: Build with Fortnite's default asset library — no licensed IP, no brand rules, no revenue share.
provides: Full access to Fortnite's standard galleries, props, and devices with no theming constraints.

sections.title: What you're allowed to build with
rules: Fortnite's own library — every standard gallery, prop, device, weapon and cosmetic is yours to use.
Your own creations, yes. You can import models, textures and animations you made yourself in Blender, Maya, Unreal Engine, Sketchfab or Quixel.

Paid Fab assets, yes. You can buy assets from Fab (Epic's marketplace) and use them in your island. Look for the UEFN tag so you know it's been made to work in Fortnite, and pick the licence tier that matches your situation — 'Personal' if you've earned under $100k in the last 12 months, 'Professional' if over.
Credit anything you didn't make. Whatever the licence, you have to list third-party assets on your island's attribution screen when you publish.
256 MB cap. All your imported and Fab content added together has to stay under 256 MB or the island won't deploy.

Music is the big exception. You must own every right to any music you upload — you wrote it, performed it, recorded it, and it's not signed to a label or collecting society. In practice that rules out commercial tracks.

sections.title: What you get paid
rules: Engagement payouts. Epic puts 40% of the eligible net revenue from Fortnite's Item Shop and other real-money purchases into a monthly pool, shared between islands based on playtime, how many players come back, and new or returning players you bring to Fortnite. You keep your full share — no rights holder takes a cut.

Selling items for V-Bucks. Normally you keep 50% of the V-Bucks value, which works out to roughly 37% of what the player actually paid. Right now Epic is running a promotion until 31 January 2027 where you keep 100% of the V-Bucks value — roughly 74% of retail.
To earn either, you need to be 18 or over and enrolled in the Fortnite Developer Program. Payouts land 30 days after the end of each month.

sections.title: Rules every island has to follow
rules: Be original. Don't copy someone else's island, and don't use characters, art, music or logos you don't own the rights to. You also can't use the Fortnite or Epic Games logos in your island.
Violence stays unrealistic. No realistic gore or blood, no death animations, no kill replays. Horror and scary themes are fine as long as they aren't intense or sustained.
Keep the language and themes mild. Occasional mild profanity is allowed; sexual expletives, hateful language, nudity and sexual content are not. No references to alcohol, tobacco or drugs at all.
No gambling. No casino-style games, raffles or games of chance for a prize — even using pretend currency.
Nothing that leaves the island. No external links, QR codes, social handles, or requests to DM you. No photos or videos of real people.
Protect players' privacy. Don't collect or ask for personal information, and don't build your own chat boxes or custom keyboards.
No bullying, harassment, or discrimination of any kind.
Be honest in your listing. Your title, thumbnail and description must match what's actually in your island. Don't promise XP, V-Bucks or rewards, and don't use terms like 'AFK' or 'XP farm'.
Keep it technically sound. Stay above 30 FPS and make sure it's playable on every platform Fortnite supports — you can't ship mobile-only.
Rate it honestly. You'll fill in an IARC age-rating questionnaire when you publish; declare any violence, scares, language or in-island purchases truthfully.

sections.title: What you're allowed to build with
rules: Provided assets only, used as provided. You can't import your own Star Wars-style assets, invent new ones, or extract/copy the provided ones outside UEFN.
Your island must contain at least one Star Wars asset to count as a Star Wars island.

Kitbashing is allowed for scenery only. You can combine architecture, props and terrain into new structures — but characters, vehicles and weapons are 'Hero Assets' and must be used exactly as provided, with no stretching, recolouring or combining.

Your own assets are allowed, with two hard exclusions: no IP derived from film or TV, and no characters from major game franchises — even if you own the rights to them. This is stricter than the other brands.

Star Wars music is on a borrowed clock. You get licensed tracks and 230+ sound effects, but you may only change length, volume and looping — no remixes, pitch shifts or lyrics. When the licence expires you can keep an already-published island live, but you won't be able to publish any further updates to it while it still contains that music.
No mixing with other IP, including other branded templates, even with the rights holder's permission.

sections.title: What you get paid
rules: 20% of your engagement payout goes to Disney, deducted automatically before you're paid.

Star Wars is the only brand that supports selling items for V-Bucks — but 30% of that revenue also goes to Disney. Offers only work inside your own Star Wars islands, and can't be built from sound effects or music alone.

You need to opt in first. Join the Fortnite Developer Program and sign the IP Partner Licensing Agreement in the Creator Portal. One signature covers every branded template, so if you've done it for another brand you're already set.

sections.title: Rules specific to this brand
rules: You must include this line in your island description: "Portions of the materials used are trademarks and/or copyrighted works of The Walt Disney Company. All rights reserved by Disney. This material is not official and is not endorsed by Disney."

You can use 'Star Wars' plus location and character names in your island title, as long as you don't imply Disney made or endorsed it. You can't use any Star Wars or Disney logo, any Disney company name (Lucasfilm, Marvel, Pixar), or any existing game/film title such as Battlefront, Outlaws or Jedi: Fallen Order.
No actor names or likenesses in your thumbnail, description, videos or anything you sell.

Nothing political, religious or military. Don't pair Star Wars assets with religious icons, real-world flags or uniforms, and don't use them to advertise products or take a position on real-world issues.

Anything new you build from Star Wars assets belongs to Disney. The rules require you to assign rights in any 'Disney Derivative Work' to Disney — your own pre-existing IP and generic gameplay systems are carved out.
Enforced by Epic and Disney. Disney can report your island directly.

settings.name: Winning Team
settings.default: There's no single 'win condition' field — wire an event from Round Settings, Score Manager, or a Tracker into this device once your win condition is met, and set Winning Team from that event.

settings.name: Game End Callout
settings.default: Options: You Win/Lose / Placement / Cooperative. You Win/Lose for team vs team, Placement for FFA/battle-royale style.

Sky Dome.purpose: Controls sky, lighting mood, fog, and atmosphere — the fastest way to make an island feel intentional rather than default.

settings.name: Light Source
settings.default: Options: None / Sun / Moon 1 / Moon 2. Sun for daytime, Moon for a night scene.

settings.name: Skydome Top/Middle/Bottom Color
settings.default: Match your mood — stormy/dark for horror, bright for racing.

settings.name: Horizon Fog Density
settings.default: Higher for limited visibility/tension, lower for open exploration.

Customizable Light.purpose: Adds and colors light sources to set mood in specific areas.

settings.name: Light Color
settings.default: Match your mood — cold blue/green for horror, warm for cozy scenes.

settings.name: Rhythm Preset
settings.default: Options: Constant / Flicker / Wave / Short Circuit / Party / Windy / Flash. Flicker suits horror tension.

settings.name: Light Intensity
settings.default: Dim for tension, bright for clarity in puzzle areas.

Audio Player.purpose: Layers in ambience, music, or stingers — sound design does as much for atmosphere as visuals.

settings.name: Audio
settings.default: Pick the ambience/music/stinger sound asset for this moment.

settings.name: Can be Heard By
settings.default: Options: Everyone / Instigator Only / Registered Players Only / Non-Registered Players Only. Everyone for ambience, Instigator Only for personal SFX.

settings.name: Enable Spatialization
settings.default: True for a 3D-positioned sound, False for flat background music.

Score Manager.purpose: Tracks eliminations/points per player or team.

settings.name: Score Value
settings.default: Set the point value per elimination/objective (default 1).

settings.name: Score Award Type
settings.default: Options: None / Add / Subtract / Set. Add for an ongoing tally, Set to force a specific value.

settings.name: Activating Team
settings.default: Set to whichever team/player triggers a score change.

Round Settings.purpose: Controls per-round inventory reset and, via 'Last Standing Wins', the classic elimination-style win condition.

settings.name: Last Standing Wins
settings.default: On, for an elimination-style win condition (last player/team standing wins the round). Toggle via 'Override Last Standing Wins' first.

settings.name: Round
settings.default: Set which round number(s) this configuration applies to, or All.

settings.name: Keep Items Between Rounds
settings.default: Off for a fresh loadout each round, On for persistent progress.

Team Settings and Inventory.purpose: Assigns players to teams and configures per-team starting inventory.

settings.name: Max Initial Team Size
settings.default: Set to your intended squad size (e.g. 1 for solos, 2 for duos, 4 for full squads).

settings.name: Team
settings.default: Set which team number this configuration applies to.

settings.name: Respawn Type
settings.default: Options: Individual / Wave. Individual for standard respawns, Wave for round-based team respawns.

Class Designer.purpose: Defines a custom class with a preset inventory loadout.

settings.name: Class Name
settings.default: Give it a clear, thematic name players will recognize.

settings.name: Max Health
settings.default: Adjust only if this class should be tankier/less tanky than default.

settings.name: Allow Building
settings.default: Options: None / All / Traps Only / No Traps. Match your genre — e.g. No Traps for box fights.

Class and Team Selector.purpose: Controls which classes are available to which players/teams.

settings.name: Class to Switch To
settings.default: Pick the Class Designer class this selector assigns.

settings.name: Team To Switch To
settings.default: Pick the team this selector assigns, if any.

settings.name: Clear Items On Switch
settings.default: Options: Never / Team / Class / Always. Always gives a clean reset on switch.

Item Spawner.purpose: Spawns pickup weapons/resources around the map.

settings.name: Item List > Item Definition
settings.default: Choose weapons/resources appropriate to your game's power level.

settings.name: Time Between Spawns
settings.default: Short for a high-loot game, long for scarcity-driven tension (paired with Respawn Item On Timer).

settings.name: Random Spawns
settings.default: Options: Off / Random / No Repeats. Random adds variety across multiple spawners.

settings.name: Reset Inventory
settings.default: Off for parkour/racing (keep progress), On for elimination round resets.

settings.name: Activating Team
settings.default: Restrict to the relevant team, or leave open if shared.

settings.name: Enabled During Phase
settings.default: Match your game's phase structure (e.g. Gameplay Only).

Barrier.purpose: Blocks movement and weapon fire at the play area edge.

settings.name: Zone Shape
settings.default: Options: Box / Hollow Box / Cylinder. Match your play area's shape.

settings.name: Barrier Material
settings.default: Translucent (Red) for a visible boundary players understand, or another style for a hidden kill-box.

settings.name: Block Weapon Fire
settings.default: On, so the barrier fully blocks the boundary.

Basic Storm Controller.purpose: Simple single-phase shrinking storm; use for a lightweight zone.

settings.name: Initial Radius
settings.default: Set to your starting safe-zone size (default 50M).

settings.name: Final Radius
settings.default: Set to 0 (or a small end-circle) so the zone fully closes.

settings.name: Damage Level
settings.default: Higher forces players in faster; keep low for a casual mode.

Advanced Storm Controller.purpose: Multi-phase (up to 50) storm for more tuned pacing; alternative to Basic Storm Controller.

settings.name: Phase One Radius
settings.default: Set to your map's starting safe-zone size (default 200M, range 5-5000M).

settings.name: Use Custom Storm Phases
settings.default: Yes, if you're placing Advanced Storm Beacon devices to customize individual phases.

settings.name: Bounds Radius
settings.default: Set to your overall play-area radius (default 200M).

Advanced Storm Beacon.purpose: Customizes individual phases of the Advanced Storm Controller.

settings.name: Phase
settings.default: Set to the phase number (2-50) you want this beacon to override.

settings.name: Storm Radius
settings.default: Set the safe-zone size for this phase (has no effect if Phase = 1).

settings.name: Damage Level
settings.default: Ramp this up on later phases — e.g. 5% early on, 25%+ or Instant Elimination by the final phase.

Reboot Van.purpose: Lets players bring eliminated teammates back into the game.

settings.name: Recharge Time
settings.default: Shorter (below 30s default) for a fast-paced game, longer for a slower-burn match.

settings.name: Reboot Progress Delay
settings.default: Options: Custom Decay / Instant Reset / Battle Royale. Instant Reset for quick reboots.

Disguise.purpose: Core mechanic - lets Hiders transform into a prop cosmetically.

settings.name: Disguise to Apply
settings.default: Pick a prop/cosmetic that blends into the environment players are hiding in.

settings.name: Disguise Breaks on Damage
settings.default: Options: On Damaged / On Damaged By Opponent / On DBNO / On Eliminated / Off. On Damaged By Opponent so only real hits break cover.

settings.name: Team to Apply To
settings.default: Restrict to the Hiders team.

Timer.purpose: Round countdown for the hide/seek phase.

settings.name: Duration
settings.default: Set to your intended round/escape/race time limit (default 1 min).

settings.name: Count Down Direction
settings.default: Options: Count Down / Count Up. Count Down for a time-limited objective, Count Up for a race/best-time stopwatch.

settings.name: Completion Behavior
settings.default: Options: Disable / Stop / Reset / Restart. Match what should happen when time runs out.

Item Granter.purpose: Grants Seekers a specific weapon at round start.

settings.name: On Grant Action
settings.default: Options: Clear Inventory / Clear Items / Clear Resources / Keep All. Keep All to add to existing inventory, Clear Inventory for a fresh loadout.

settings.name: Item List > Item Definition
settings.default: Set to the specific weapon/reward for this moment.

settings.name: Item List > Item Quantity
settings.default: Set ammo/stack size to match how long the reward should last.

settings.name: Message
settings.default: Write the instruction/status update players need at this moment.

settings.name: Display Time
settings.default: Long enough to read comfortably, short enough not to block the view (default 5 sec).

settings.name: Message Recipient
settings.default: Options: All / Friendlies / Enemies / Triggering Player / a specific team. Target the relevant role when the message is role-specific.

Stat Creator.purpose: Creates the custom currency stat that drives the whole tycoon loop.

settings.name: Stat Name
settings.default: Name it clearly (e.g. 'Gold', 'BestTime', 'QuestProgress').

settings.name: Scope
settings.default: Options: Player / Team / Match. Player for individual stats, Team/Match for shared trackers.

settings.name: Max Value
settings.default: Set only if this stat should drive a level-up system (pairs with Max Level).

Stat Powerup.purpose: Grants or deducts the currency stat when triggered (earning/spending).

settings.name: Stat To Apply
settings.default: Point this to your custom Stat Creator stat (or a built-in stat like Score).

settings.name: Magnitude
settings.default: Set how much currency/progress this grants or deducts per trigger (default 1).

settings.name: Apply To
settings.default: Player, unless the reward should be shared with their team/class.

Tracker.purpose: Displays the player's currency/progress on their HUD.

settings.name: Stat to Track
settings.default: Link to a custom Stat Creator stat, or a built-in stat like Eliminations/Score.

settings.name: Target Value
settings.default: Set to the win/completion threshold, if any (default 10).

settings.name: When Target Is Reached
settings.default: Options: Do Nothing / End Round / Complete Tracker. End Round if reaching the target should win.

settings.name: Times Can Trigger
settings.default: Infinite for repeatable purchases, a fixed number for a one-time unlock.

settings.name: Reset Delay
settings.default: Add a short delay (a few seconds) to prevent spam-clicking.

settings.name: Activating Team
settings.default: Restrict to the team that should interact, or leave Any.

Collectible Object.purpose: Placeable pickup (coins/tokens) that grants currency on collection.

settings.name: Collectible Object
settings.default: Pick a coin/token/gem visual that matches your theme.

settings.name: Score
settings.default: Set to the currency/stat amount awarded per pickup (default 1).

settings.name: Consume if Collected By
settings.default: Options: Self / Anyone / Team. Self for individual collection, Team to share credit.

Elimination Manager.purpose: Grants currency-equivalent items/stat when an agent is eliminated.

settings.name: Number of Items Dropped
settings.default: Set to how much loot you want dropped on elimination (default All).

settings.name: Target Type
settings.default: Players Only, unless you also want creature eliminations to drop loot.

settings.name: Random Drop
settings.default: Options: Off / Random / No Repeats. Off for guaranteed drops, Random for variety.

Vending Machine.purpose: Sells up to 3 items for a currency cost.

settings.name: First Item Resource Type
settings.default: Pick the currency type players will spend (Wood/Stone/Metal/Gold).

settings.name: Cost of First Item
settings.default: Balance against how fast players earn that currency.

Conditional Button.purpose: Only activates the upgrade if the player has enough currency/required items.

settings.name: Number of Key Item Slots
settings.default: 1 for a simple cost, 2-3 for a multi-item requirement.

settings.name: Key Items Required
settings.default: Set to the quantity of the currency/key item needed.

settings.name: Consume Key Items
settings.default: On for a one-time purchase, Off for a repeatable check.

Prop Mover.purpose: Moves building pieces/walls to reveal new base areas on upgrade.

settings.name: Movement Mode
settings.default: Options: Translation / Rotation. Translation for a sliding wall/platform, Rotation for a spinning/turning door.

settings.name: Speed
settings.default: Slow enough to look intentional, fast enough not to feel sluggish.

settings.name: Path Complete Action
settings.default: Options: None / Ping Pong / Repeat / Reset. Match whether this should move once, loop, or reset.

Prop Manipulator.purpose: Defines a zone that overrides resource-node behavior and/or prop health/destructibility for props inside it (not a direct push/pull/move device — that's Prop Mover).

settings.name: Override Resources
settings.default: On, if this zone should change how resource nodes behave inside it.

settings.name: Modify Prop Health
settings.default: On, then set Prop Health if you want props more/less durable in this zone.

settings.name: Affects All Objects In a Zone
settings.default: On to affect everything in the zone, Off to target only tagged props.

Trick Tile.purpose: Trap tile that destroys itself (and drops the player) when activated.

settings.name: Trigger on Player Contact
settings.default: Yes, for a classic deathrun trap.

settings.name: Activation Delay
settings.default: A short delay (e.g. 2 seconds or less) so it feels reactive, not instant.

settings.name: Reset After
settings.default: Set a reset time if the trap should reappear; Never if it's a one-time trap.

Damage Volume.purpose: Hazard area that damages/eliminates players who touch it.

settings.name: Damage
settings.default: High enough to eliminate/deter on contact for a hazard; low for a 'slow' zone (default 10).

settings.name: Damage Tick Rate
settings.default: Shorter interval (below the 2s default) is more punishing.

settings.name: Damage Type
settings.default: Options: Elimination / Damage Over Time. Elimination for an instant-kill hazard, Damage Over Time for a gentler zone.

Pinball Bumper.purpose: Knocks players off narrow paths as an obstacle.

settings.name: Knockback Player
settings.default: Strong enough to matter but not so strong players fly off the course.

settings.name: Damage
settings.default: Light chip damage for a fun bounce, higher if it should be a genuine hazard (default None).

settings.name: Bumper Color
settings.default: Options: Blue / Blue Glow / Red / Silver / Pink Glow / Green Glow / Orange Glow / Gold. Match your theme.

Grind Rail.purpose: Rail section players grind along for a traversal segment.

settings.name: Visual Style
settings.default: Options: Standard / Wire / Vine / Minerail. Match your theme.

settings.name: Speed Preset
settings.default: Standard, or tune the underlying speed fields directly for a custom feel — faster for a thrill section, slower for precision.

Air Vent.purpose: Boosts players upward through the course.

settings.name: Knockup Force Multiplier
settings.default: Options: None / Low / Medium / High / Very High / Super High / Mega High. Pick High or above to clear the gap/height you designed.

settings.name: Enable on Phase
settings.default: Options: None / Always / Pre-Game Only / Gameplay Only / Create Only. Always unless it should only work during a specific phase.

settings.name: Bounce Launch Value
settings.default: Tune above the 16 m/s default to clear the height/gap you designed.

settings.name: Bounce Direction
settings.default: Options: Bouncer Orientation / Vertical. Vertical for a straight-up launch.

settings.name: Is Indestructible
settings.default: True if it shouldn't be shot/broken; otherwise set Device Health.

Teleporter.purpose: Returns a failed player to their last checkpoint.

settings.name: Teleporter Group
settings.default: Link this Teleporter to its matching exit via a shared group.

settings.name: Change Teleporter Target
settings.default: Options: Never / On Entry / On Timer. Never for a fixed link, On Timer for a rotating destination.

HUD Controller.purpose: Hides HUD elements (map, health bar, etc.) to increase immersion/tension.

settings.name: Show HUD Messages / Show Minimap / etc.
settings.default: Set the specific HUD elements to No for immersion-focused genres like horror (each is its own Do Not Override / Yes / No dropdown).

settings.name: Enabled During Phase
settings.default: All, unless it should only apply during a specific phase.

Lock.purpose: Locks a door until the player has the right key/item/condition.

settings.name: Starts Locked
settings.default: Locked, for gated content.

settings.name: Initial Door Position
settings.default: Closed, to match a locked door.

Attribute Evaluator.purpose: Checks whether a puzzle condition is met (e.g. correct items collected) and fires pass/fail events.

settings.name: Tracked Stat
settings.default: Set to Score, or point it at your custom Stat Creator stat representing puzzle/quest progress.

settings.name: Min Player Stat
settings.default: Set to the threshold value that counts as 'solved'.

settings.name: Times Can Trigger
settings.default: Infinite, unless the check should only ever pass/fail once.

settings.name: Initial State
settings.default: Off, for a puzzle that needs solving.

settings.name: Limit Times Can Change
settings.default: On, then set Times Can Change if this should only be usable once or a few times.

settings.name: Mutually Exclusive
settings.default: Group switches that should only allow one 'on' at a time (e.g. a 3-lever puzzle).

Conversation.purpose: Branching narrative dialogue built via the Conversation Graph.

settings.name: Conversation
settings.default: Build the dialogue tree in the Conversation Graph editor (a Conversation Bank asset), then link it here.

settings.name: Conversation Type
settings.default: Options: Radial / Box / Custom. Radial for quick prompts, Box for longer scripted dialogue.

Popup Dialog.purpose: Simple HUD text boxes for clues/choices.

settings.name: Description
settings.default: Write the clue/choice text for this moment.

settings.name: Response Type
settings.default: Add more buttons (up to 12) if the player's answer should branch.

settings.name: Auto Display
settings.default: Options: Never / Pregame Lobby / Game Start. Game Start if it should appear automatically.

Creature Placer.purpose: Spawns the chaser NPC at a fixed location or on trigger.

settings.name: Creature Type
settings.default: Choose the specific chaser/enemy creature for this encounter.

settings.name: Enable on Game Phase
settings.default: Options: Never / Game Countdown / Game Start. Game Start for a standard encounter.

settings.name: Despawn Type
settings.default: Options: Distance To Enemy / Distance To Spawner / Do Not Despawn. Distance To Enemy for a persistent chaser.

AI Patrol Path Node.purpose: Defines a patrol route so the chaser doesn't stay static.

settings.name: Patrolling Mode
settings.default: Options: Back and Forth / Looping / Stop at End. Use Looping for a continuous patrol route.

settings.name: Enabled at Start
settings.default: On, so the patrol begins immediately when the game starts.

Perception Trigger.purpose: Detects when the chaser has line-of-sight to the player to escalate tension/attacks.

settings.name: Activating Team
settings.default: Restrict to the team you want this to detect (e.g. Hiders), or leave Any.

settings.name: Delay
settings.default: Add a short delay so detection doesn't feel instant/unfair.

settings.name: Enabled on Game Start
settings.default: On.

Volume.purpose: Used as checkpoint gates around the track to validate lap progress.

settings.name: Volume Shape
settings.default: Options: Box / Cylinder / Sphere. Match the shape of the checkpoint gate or area you're detecting.

settings.name: Player Events Enabled
settings.default: On, so player Enter/Exit actually fires events.

settings.name: Volume Width/Depth/Height
settings.default: Size to fully cover the area you're detecting.

Vehicle Spawner (specific type, e.g. Spo.purpose: Spawns the chosen race vehicle for each player.

settings.name: Activating Team
settings.default: Restrict to the racer's team, or leave Any.

settings.name: Enable Respawn
settings.default: On, if vehicles can be destroyed/flipped and need to respawn.

settings.name: Vehicle Speed Tunings
settings.default: Pick the tuning (e.g. Ch 4 Battle Royale) that matches your race's intended speed/handling feel. Note: exact property names vary slightly between vehicle types (e.g. Sedan vs Sports Car), so double-check against the specific spawner you place.

Player Movement Settings.purpose: Adjusts a player's movement speed/jump for a faster-paced on-foot race.

settings.name: Walk Maximum Speed
settings.default: Increase above 'Don't Override' for a faster-paced foot race or traversal game.

settings.name: Jump Velocity
settings.default: Raise above 'Don't Override' if your course/game relies on higher jumps than default.

settings.name: Category Filter
settings.default: Filter to just the movement categories you're actually tuning (e.g. Walking, Jumping).

Nitro Hoop.purpose: Flaming hoop that grants a nitro speed boost when passed through.

settings.name: Added Player Velocity
settings.default: Tune above the 45 m/s default for the straightaway it's placed on.

settings.name: Enable Cooldown
settings.default: On, to prevent back-to-back boosting if the hoop is on a lap loop.

Nitro Barrel Spawner.purpose: Destructible barrel prop that grants a nitro boost.

settings.name: Launch Force Multiplier
settings.default: Match your track's boost balance (default 1.0) — too much trivializes corners.

settings.name: Should Respawn
settings.default: On for a repeatable boost, Off for a one-time pickup.

Physics Boulder.purpose: Rolling obstacle that can damage/knock racers off course.

settings.name: Health
settings.default: High enough to survive normal fights; low if it should be easily destroyed to disable the trap (default 180).

settings.name: Damage to Players
settings.default: High enough to threaten (default 150); lower if it's a repeatable hazard.

settings.name: Timed Respawn
settings.default: Set a respawn time (e.g. 15m) if the trap should reset.

Fuel Pump.purpose: Refuels vehicles at pit stops along the track.

settings.name: Fuel Capacity
settings.default: Full (default 1000) for casual play, lower for tighter fuel management.

settings.name: Explosion Deals Damage
settings.default: Yes if it should be a hazard when destroyed.

settings.name: Fuel Refill Percentage Per Restore Tick
settings.default: Faster (raise above the 5% default) for arcade-y racing, slower if fuel management should matter strategically.

settings.name: Damageable
settings.default: No, if it should be indestructible infrastructure.

NPC Spawner.purpose: Spawns quest-giver or friendly NPCs from a Character Definition asset.

settings.name: NPC Character Definition
settings.default: Build the NPC's look/behavior in a Character Definition asset, then link it here.

settings.name: Spawn Character at Game Start
settings.default: On, for a persistent quest-giver NPC.

settings.name: Total Spawn Limit
settings.default: Cap it so quest-giver NPCs don't overpopulate the area.

Creature Spawner.purpose: Spawns waves of enemy creatures at intervals.

settings.name: Number of Creatures
settings.default: Set to how many creatures spawn per wave (default 4).

settings.name: Wave Timer
settings.default: Space waves out enough for players to catch their breath.

settings.name: Creature Type
settings.default: Mix types for variety in later waves.

Creature Manager.purpose: Tunes creature health/damage/drops for difficulty scaling.

settings.name: Creature Type
settings.default: Pick the creature/wildlife type this manager should tune (e.g. Fiend).

settings.name: Health
settings.default: Scale up for later waves/harder difficulty, down for early encounters.

settings.name: Affected Creatures
settings.default: Options: New Creatures Only / New and Existing Creatures. Pick the latter to apply retroactively.

Save Point.purpose: Saves and loads a player's inventory, class, team, and stats across sessions.

settings.name: Auto-Load Behavior
settings.default: Every Spawn, so returning players always pick up where they left off.

settings.name: Save Loadout
settings.default: On, if class/inventory should persist across sessions.

Multi-phase shrinking zone that drives the core Zone Wars pressure.
Tracks round wins per squad.

questions.prompt: What squad size - solos, duos, or full squads?
Allow teammates to be revived/rebooted after elimination?
